message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command that brings up the Docker Engine (the Docker Desktop service).  
It is used to start **containers** that have already been created.  

If you want to start the Docker Desktop service itself on Windows, you need to start the underlying Windows service that runs the Docker Engine. Here are the most common ways to do that:

| Method | Command | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| **PowerShell (recommended)** | `Start-Service Docker` | Run PowerShell as **Administrator**. This starts the `Docker Desktop Service` (`com.docker.service`). |
| **Command Prompt** | `net start com.docker.service` | Same effect as the PowerShell command. |
| **Docker Desktop GUI** | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon | The GUI will automatically start the service if it isn’t running. |

### Example: Starting Docker via PowerShell

```powershell
# Open PowerShell as Administrator
Start-Service Docker
```

### Example: Starting Docker via Command Prompt

```cmd
net start com.docker.service
```

### Starting a Container

If you actually meant to start a **container**, you would first need to know its name or ID, then run:

```bash
docker start <container_name_or_id>
```

Replace `<container_name_or_id>` with the actual name or ID of the container you want to start.

---

#### Quick One‑liner (PowerShell)

If you prefer a single line that you can paste into PowerShell:

```powershell
Start-Service Docker
```

#### Quick One‑liner (Command Prompt)

```cmd
net start com.docker.service
```

---

**Tip:**  
If you’re using Docker Desktop, you can also start it from the system tray icon or by launching the Docker Desktop application. Once the service is running, you can then use `docker ps`, `docker run`, etc., to manage containers.
